items.headline: Databricks open-sources Omnigent, a meta-harness wrapping Claude Code, Codex and agent SDKs behind one interface
items.diff_narrative: A new agent-tooling storyline opens that had no presence yesterday. Databricks introduced Omnigent on June 13, an Apache-2.0 alpha meta-harness that sits above individual coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Pi) and SDKs (OpenAI Agents, Claude Agents SDK) so implementations can be swapped behind a common interface, with meta-layer policies enforcing cost budgets, permissions and OS-level sandboxing, plus shareable-by-URL live sessions for collaborative review across web, mobile, a macOS app and APIs. It is published as a standalone OSS project on GitHub timed to the Data + AI Summit rather than as a Databricks-only feature.

items.headline: A cached-rollout RL recipe trains small tool-calling agents toward frontier accuracy at a fraction of the compute
items.diff_narrative: The local-model slot turns over to a different research thread. Yesterday it was Unsloth's 150-PR 2026.6.7 beta packaging DiffusionGemma training, Gemma 4 multi-token prediction, audio chat and QAT into one local app; that release is gone today. In its place is CacheRL (arXiv:2606.14179, June 12), which replaces expensive live tool execution during reinforcement learning with a three-tier fuzzy cache of replayed trajectories plus a cache-tier-aware hybrid reward, reporting 92% process accuracy against GPT-5's 94% at roughly 100x less compute and lifting Qwen3-4B-Thinking validation reward from 0.43 to 0.78. The angle shifts from packaging an on-device fine-tuning app to a concrete method for distilling tool-calling competence into a small model without a live-execution RL loop.

items.headline: AI events to plan around now: the Databricks Data + AI Summit opens at Moscone
items.diff_narrative: The three-track calendar (mainstream dev/data, AI-security, AI-chip) holds, but several anchors firm up as the summer fills in. The Databricks Data + AI Summit is now live, opening today and running June 15-18, with the lineup detail shifting from the June 17 Chainsmokers show at Oracle Park to a multi-day OpenAI hackathon. AMD's Advancing AI tightens from a June 22-23 window to a single locked July 23 date; Black Hat USA's AI Summit is now placed broadly inside the August 1-6 conference rather than pinned to a specific day; and OWASP Global AppSec USA narrows from November 2-6 to November 5-6. The Confidential Computing Summit (June 23-24), AI Engineer World's Fair, Hot Chips, and the AI Infra Summit carry forward unchanged.
